description: A mark that links somewhere shows the pointer, there being nothing else about it that looks clickable — and **three places can say it links**. `cursor(markDef, encoding, config)` asks `encoding.href || markDef.href || getMarkPropOrConfig('href', markDef, config)`, so a theme that gives every bar the same link makes every bar clickable, exactly as an `href` channel or an `href` on the mark would. This compiler read only the channel, so a themed link drew no pointer and the reader had nothing to tell them the mark could be followed. Both guards run through the chain too: `const specifiedCursor = getMarkPropOrConfig('cursor', markDef, config); if (specifiedCursor === undefined) { … }`, so a `cursor` the theme settles suppresses the pointer exactly as one on the mark does. The first row takes its link from `config.mark`; the second states its own `cursor` and must keep it, the theme's link notwithstanding; the third has no link at all and must have no cursor.
